description_full: Liquidity Services, Inc. engages in the provision of e-commerce marketplaces, self-directed auction listing tools, and value-added services in the United States and internationally. The company operates through four segments: GovDeals, Retail Supply Chain Group (RSCG), Capital Assets Group (CAG), and Machinio. Its solutions enable government entities and commercial businesses to sell surplus property and real estate assets through GovDeals, Bid4Assets, and Sierra marketplaces. The company also offers a suite of services, including surplus management, asset valuation, asset sales, marketing, returns management, asset recovery, and ecommerce services; and operates Liquidation.com, a marketplace to sell excess, returned, and overstocked consumer goods. In addition, it operates a global search engine platform for listing used equipment for sale in the construction, machine tool, transportation, printing, laboratory/medical, and agriculture sectors. Further, the company provides Machinio System service that offers various software tools, such as website hosting, email marketing, and inventory management to equipment sellers. The company offers products for various industries, such as consumer electronics, general merchandise, apparel, scientific equipment, aerospace parts and equipment, technology hardware, real estate, energy equipment, industrial capital assets, heavy equipment, fleet and transportation equipment, and specialty equipment. It also operates an online auction marketplace platform that connects auction houses with clients offering services, such as account registration, bidding on auction items, and notifications for auction reminders and outbid alerts through its mobile application for iOS and Android devices. The company was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland.

financial_summary: Liquidity Services, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.4B market cap on $477M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 51% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $59M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.38× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -10.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 9.4%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 5.97).
It runs a 51% gross margin and converts 12% of revenue into free cash flow, or 9% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 2.38x, but high accruals (-10.3% of assets).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $231.1M (14% of market cap).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 19.4% over 3 years, 18.3% over 5 years and 1.8% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 21%).
At current returns, reinvesting 66% of profits supports about 8.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 36.8% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.7x depreciation (1.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 28, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 24.8%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 81%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (18 sales, net $3.8M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.2% (1.2% in buybacks).

people: With about 818 employees, each generates about $583K of revenue, 1.5x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 2.7% a year.

The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
